previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission following allogeneic stem cell transplant and severe chronic graft-versus-host disease was admitted for fever and cough. He met SIRS criteria on admission with tachycardia and fever. Initial chest imaging showed a small right pleural effusion and atelectasis, with no pulmonary embolism on CTA. Respiratory viral panels, blood cultures, and Legionella testing were negative. He was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics including vancomycin, meropenem, and levofloxacin. Due to MRSA colonization and evolving ground-glass opacities on CT, antibiotics were adjusted, with meropenem briefly restarted and IVIG administered. His fever resolved, tachycardia improved with reduced levothyroxine, and he was de-escalated to levofloxacin monotherapy. His chronic conditions, including systolic heart failure, hypothyroidism, and lower extremity wounds, were managed supportively. He was discharged home on levofloxacin with plans to restart prior prophylactic antibiotics, obtain outpatient CT imaging, and follow up with cardiology and oncology.
